sentences.en: This is 99% Invisible.
sentences.zh: 这里是《99%隐形》。

sentences.en: I'm Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: 我是罗曼·马尔斯。

sentences.en: If you live in an American city, and you walk outside to a major intersection and look into the streets,
sentences.zh: 如果你住在美国城市，走到外面的主要路口，往街道里看，

sentences.en: you know what you'll see.
sentences.zh: 你就知道你会看到什么。

sentences.en: You'll see cars, and trucks, and buses.
sentences.zh: 你会看到汽车、卡车和公交车。

sentences.en: You might see a few bicycles trying to sneak their way through the traffic.
sentences.zh: 你可能会看到几辆自行车试图在车流中穿行。

sentences.en: What you won't see are people.
sentences.zh: 你看不到的是人。

sentences.en: Not on the street anyway.
sentences.zh: 至少在街道上是这样。

sentences.en: Maybe on the sidewalk, waiting for their turn to cross,
sentences.zh: 也许在人行道上，等着过马路，

sentences.en: and then crossing quickly, hurrying to get out of the way so that the cars can get going again.
sentences.zh: 然后快速穿过，匆忙避让，好让汽车继续通行。

sentences.en: In recent times, some of us have come to think the city streets shouldn't just be for cars and trucks.
sentences.zh: 近来，我们中的一些人开始认为城市街道不应该只属于汽车和卡车。

sentences.en: That cars take up too much space and release too much carbon just to move a couple of people a short distance.
sentences.zh: 因为汽车占用了太多空间，为了把几个人送往短距离目的地，却排放了过多的碳。

sentences.en: But even those anti-car haters, and I am one, we know the streets belong to our enemy.
sentences.zh: 但即使是那些反车族——我也是其中之一——我们也知道街道属于我们的敌人。

sentences.en: We look both ways before crossing.
sentences.zh: 我们过马路前会左右看。

sentences.en: We don't let our children play in the streets.
sentences.zh: 我们不让孩子在街上玩耍。

sentences.en: We might sometimes jaywalk, cross the street at the wrong place or time.
sentences.zh: 我们有时可能会乱穿马路，在错误的时间或地点过街。

sentences.en: But we know in our heart of hearts, we're in the wrong.
sentences.zh: 但我们内心深处知道，我们做错了。

sentences.en: Scofflaws.
sentences.zh: 藐视法律的人。

sentences.en: That's our reporter, Jesse Dukes.
sentences.zh: 那是我们的记者，杰西·杜克斯。

sentences.en: Because I actually love cars, but I just don't think they make sense in the city.
sentences.zh: 因为我其实很喜欢汽车，只是觉得它们在城市里并不合理。

sentences.en: And this is a story about jaywalking.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于“乱穿马路”的故事。

sentences.en: Where that word jaywalking came from, and how it was a weapon in a turf war
sentences.zh: 这个词是怎么来的，以及它是如何成为一场地盘争夺战的武器，

sentences.en: between the people who wanted cars in the streets and everybody else.
sentences.zh: 在这场争夺战中，一方是想要汽车占领街道的人，另一方是其他人。

sentences.en: You can probably guess who won.
sentences.zh: 你大概能猜到谁赢了。

sentences.en: All right, there's a wonderful cartoon in the St. Louis Post-Dispatch from 1923.
sentences.zh: 好的，1923年的《圣路易斯邮报》上有一幅精彩的漫画。

sentences.en: It's called The Modern Moloch.
sentences.zh: 它叫《现代摩洛克》。

sentences.en: And Moloch was a deity of the Ammonites.
sentences.zh: 摩洛克是亚扪人崇拜的神。

sentences.en: And this is Peter Norton, a historian at the University of Virginia who studies city streets.
sentences.zh: 这位是彼得·诺顿，弗吉尼亚大学研究城市街道的历史学家。

sentences.en: Moloch was a deity to whom the Ammonites sacrificed their own children in return for prosperity.
sentences.zh: 摩洛克是亚扪人为了换取繁荣而献祭自己孩子的神。

sentences.en: What an image for what the car was.
sentences.zh: 对于汽车的本质来说，这真是个绝妙的隐喻。

sentences.en: Because the idea is that we're sacrificing our children in the name of modern technology.
sentences.zh: 因为这个观点是，我们正以现代科技的名义牺牲我们的孩子。

sentences.en: According to Peter Norton, there was a time in the 1920s when it looked like public opinion was against having cars in the streets.
sentences.zh: 据彼得·诺顿所说，在20世纪20年代，曾有一段时间，公众舆论似乎反对让汽车进入街道。

sentences.en: In this particular cartoon, you see a driver kneeling at an altar, which is the front grill of a car,
sentences.zh: 在这幅特定的漫画中，你看到一个司机跪在祭坛前，而祭坛就是汽车的前格栅，

sentences.en: with a huge bowl full of the corpses of children, offering it up to the mouth of this machine beast as a sacrifice.
sentences.zh: 上面放着一个巨大的碗，装满了孩子们的尸体，作为祭品献给这台机械野兽的嘴里。

sentences.en: It's a very striking cartoon.
sentences.zh: 这是一幅非常震撼的漫画。

sentences.en: And it may seem a little bizarre to us today until you recognize that this thing was killing thousands of children every year.
sentences.zh: 在今天看来这可能有点离奇，直到你意识到这东西每年都在杀死成千上万的孩子。

sentences.en: So that was 1923, 90 years ago.
sentences.zh: 那是1923年，90年前的事了。

sentences.en: But to understand why cars were being compared to a child-eating God, we've got to go back a few more years.
sentences.zh: 但要理解为什么汽车会被比作吃孩子的神，我们得再往回追溯几年。

sentences.en: And so if you went back 100, 110 years, I think you'd be amazed to see people just strolling right into the street, any place, any time.
sentences.zh: 如果你回到100或110年前，我想你会惊讶地发现，人们随时随地都可以直接漫步到街上。

sentences.en: Sure, they'll look, but not very carefully.
sentences.zh: 当然，他们会看路，但不会特别小心。

sentences.en: At the turn of the century, there was nothing moving faster than about 5 or 10 miles an hour in the street.
sentences.zh: 世纪之交时，街上没有任何东西的速度超过每小时5到10英里。

sentences.en: Responsible parents would say to their children, go outside and play in the streets all day.
sentences.zh: 负责任的父母会告诉孩子：出去，整天在街上玩吧。

sentences.en: Even after the first cars appeared in the cities, right around 1900, they had to conform to the customs of the day, which meant that traffic moved slowly.
sentences.zh: 即使在1900年左右第一批汽车出现在城市后，它们也必须遵守当时的习俗，这意味着交通移动缓慢。

sentences.en: There's wonderful video, like 1905, people walking down Market Street in San Francisco before the earthquake.
sentences.zh: 有一段很棒的视频，大约是1905年，地震前人们走在旧金山的市场街上。

sentences.en: And people are just striding right in wherever they want to go.
sentences.zh: 人们想去哪儿就直接大步走过去。

sentences.en: So children, people carrying, you know, boards of wood, people going about their business.
sentences.zh: 所以孩子们、搬着木板的人、忙着自己事情的人都在走。

sentences.en: It's not to say that the street off of the sidewalks for everybody, because people prefer the sidewalk.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说街道对所有人来说都比人行道好，因为人们更喜欢人行道。

sentences.en: It's drier, it's cleaner, it's got less horse manure.
sentences.zh: 人行道更干燥、更干净，马粪也更少。

sentences.en: And there weren't even really many rules about what you could do or not do.
sentences.zh: 而且对于你能做什么或不能做什么，甚至没有什么真正的规则。

sentences.en: People are solving problems the way they solve problems when you're walking in a crowded hallway,
sentences.zh: 人们解决问题的方式就像在拥挤的走廊里行走时解决问题一样，

sentences.en: like, you know, in a school building between classes and you have a huge crowd of kids or something trying to find their way.
sentences.zh: 比如在学校下课期间，一大群孩子试图找到自己的路。

sentences.en: And they start to figure stuff out, like, you know, usually keep right while you're walking.
sentences.zh: 他们开始摸索出一些规律，比如，走路时通常靠右走。

sentences.en: There's not like a law, you know.
sentences.zh: 这并不是什么法律，你知道的。

sentences.en: But there's an understanding.
sentences.zh: 但有一种默契。

sentences.en: You go that way, I'll go this way, I'll keep to the right.
sentences.zh: 你走那边，我走这边，我会靠右。

sentences.en: Okay, that guy's not going to go to the right, I'll go to the left.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那个人不靠右，那我就靠左。

sentences.en: What are you from England?
sentences.zh: 你是英国来的吗？

sentences.en: And I think the closest thing we have to that now is a city park.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们现在最接近那种状态的地方是城市公园。

sentences.en: Or maybe a pedestrian mall.
sentences.zh: 或者可能是步行街。

sentences.en: You go to a city park, and you're mostly guided by understandings.
sentences.zh: 你去城市公园，主要受默契引导。

sentences.en: Understandings like you can use the park for whatever you want, provided you don't endanger other people,
sentences.zh: 默契就是你可以随心所欲地使用公园，前提是你不能危及他人，

sentences.en: you don't break the law, and you don't make a nuisance out of yourself.
sentences.zh: 不能违法，也不能惹是生非。

sentences.en: And then you're pretty much okay.
sentences.zh: 这样你就基本没问题了。

sentences.en: And it's a lot like that in streets.
sentences.zh: 街道以前也差不多是这样。

sentences.en: But by 1920, two things changed.
sentences.zh: 但到了1920年，两件事发生了变化。

sentences.en: For one, cities in America were filling up with people.
sentences.zh: 首先，美国的城市里挤满了人。

sentences.en: This was right in the midst of the Industrial Revolution, when Americans were leaving farms to move to cities to work in factories.
sentences.zh: 这正处于工业革命中期，美国人离开农场搬到城市去工厂工作。

sentences.en: Or maybe in the middle class, if they're lucky.
sentences.zh: 如果幸运的话，也许能进入中产阶级。

sentences.en: So the streets were starting to get more crowded.
sentences.zh: 所以街道开始变得更加拥挤。

sentences.en: You've probably heard of the other big change.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过另一个重大变化。

sentences.en: The Model T Ford.
sentences.zh: 福特T型车。

sentences.en: The first affordable automobile.
sentences.zh: 第一款负担得起的汽车。

sentences.en: Introduced in 1908.
Mass produced in 1913.
sentences.zh: 1913年大规模生产。

sentences.en: Price is just falling every year.
sentences.zh: 价格每年都在下降。

sentences.en: By 1920, a new Model T, without any extras, you could get for $300.
sentences.zh: 到1920年，一辆不带任何额外配置的新T型车，你只需300美元就能买到。

sentences.en: And this is really now in the reach of the working class.
sentences.zh: 这现在真的在工薪阶层的承受范围内了。

sentences.en: The people who make the Ford Model T can afford to buy it.
sentences.zh: 制造福特T型车的人自己也买得起。

sentences.en: That was a principle dear to the heart of Henry Ford.
sentences.zh: 这是亨利·福特心目中珍视的原则。

sentences.en: So by the 1920s, cities are crowding with people.
sentences.zh: 所以到了20世纪20年代，城市里挤满了人。

sentences.en: And these people are buying cars and driving cars in the streets.
sentences.zh: 这些人正在买车，并在街上开车。

sentences.en: Drivers don't want to drive 5 or 10 or 15 miles an hour, the speed at which street traffic has moved for decades.
sentences.zh: 司机们不想以每小时5、10或15英里的速度行驶，那是几十年来街道交通的速度。

sentences.en: They want to drive faster.
sentences.zh: 他们想开得更快。

sentences.en: And the pedestrians and children still linger in the streets, walking casually, like it's 1906.
sentences.zh: 而行人和孩子们仍然在街上徘徊，悠闲地走着，就像还在1906年一样。

sentences.en: And every year, more people are killed in automobile accidents.
sentences.zh: 每年都有更多的人死于交通事故。

sentences.en: The fatalities are rising.
sentences.zh: 死亡人数在上升。

sentences.en: And you can watch the curve.
sentences.zh: 你可以观察那条曲线。

sentences.en: You know, it's like climbing a mountain.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像爬山一样。

sentences.en: You're just going uphill the whole way.
sentences.zh: 你一直在上坡。

sentences.en: By 1923, you've got about 17, 18,000 people a year being killed by motor vehicles.
sentences.zh: 到1923年，每年约有17,000到18,000人死于机动车事故。

sentences.en: Three-quarters of those people are pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 其中四分之三是行人。

sentences.en: And half of the pedestrians killed in the cities are children under the age of 16.
sentences.zh: 而在城市中丧生的行人中，有一半是16岁以下的孩子。

sentences.en: And as far as the public is concerned, it's almost like they died in a war.
sentences.zh: 在公众看来，这几乎就像他们死于战争一样。

sentences.en: Parades are held in dozens of cities to commemorate the dead children.
sentences.zh: 几十个城市举行游行来纪念死去的孩子。

sentences.en: Monuments are built.
sentences.zh: 纪念碑被建立起来。

sentences.en: Mothers of children killed in the streets are given a special white star to honor their loss.
sentences.zh: 在街头丧生的孩子的母亲们被授予一枚特殊的白星，以纪念她们的损失。

sentences.en: And that's why in 1923, we see a cartoon comparing the automobile to Moloch, a god who demands the sacrifice of children for prosperity.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么在1923年，我们看到一幅漫画将汽车比作摩洛克，一个要求以牺牲孩子来换取繁荣的神。

sentences.en: And we get lots of newspaper articles and editorials saying this bloodbath has to end.
sentences.zh: 我们看到大量报纸文章和社论说这场血腥屠杀必须结束。

sentences.en: And almost all of them blame the deaths on the automobile.
sentences.zh: 而且几乎所有文章都将死亡归咎于汽车。

sentences.en: Like this from the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 就像《纽约时报》的这篇报道。

sentences.en: The horrors of war appear to be less appalling than the horrors of peace.
sentences.zh: 战争的恐怖似乎不如和平的恐怖令人震惊。

sentences.en: The automobile looms up as a far more destructive mechanism than the machine gun.
sentences.zh: 汽车作为一种破坏性机制，比机枪更令人恐惧。

sentences.en: The reckless motorist deals more death than the artilleryman.
sentences.zh: 鲁莽的驾驶者造成的死亡比炮兵更多。

sentences.en: The man in the street seems less safe than the man in the trench.
sentences.zh: 街上的人似乎比战壕里的人更不安全。

sentences.en: The greatest single lethal factor is the automobile.
sentences.zh: 最大的单一致命因素是汽车。

sentences.en: It left shambles in its wake as it coursed through 1923.
sentences.zh: 它在1923年的行进过程中留下了满目疮痍。

sentences.en: The New York Times, November 23, 1924.
And cities begin to think seriously about restricting the use of cars in the cities.
sentences.zh: 城市开始认真考虑限制在城市中使用汽车。

sentences.en: City managers look at outlawing curb parking or forcing cars to make right-angle turns around obstacles and intersections so they have to slow to a crawl.
sentences.zh: 城市管理者考虑取缔路边停车，或强迫汽车在障碍物和路口处进行直角转弯，迫使它们减速到爬行速度。

sentences.en: Now by 1923, a whole cottage industry has grown up around the automobile.
sentences.zh: 到了1923年，围绕汽车已经形成了一个完整的配套产业。

sentences.en: There are the manufacturers, of course, but also the dealers who've been making a lot of money in the last few years.
sentences.zh: 当然有制造商，还有过去几年赚了很多钱的经销商。

sentences.en: And there are motor clubs, which were precursors to AAA and make a lot of money selling memberships.
sentences.zh: 还有汽车俱乐部，它们是美国汽车协会（AAA）的前身，靠出售会员资格赚了很多钱。

sentences.en: So according to Peter Norton, there's a moment when all of these interests start to worry the city laws are going to make it so nobody in the city would want to buy a car.
sentences.zh: 所以据彼得·诺顿所说，有一个时刻，所有这些利益相关者开始担心城市法律会让城市里没人想买车。

sentences.en: And they have a collective oh crap moment.
sentences.zh: 他们经历了一个集体的“糟糕了”时刻。

sentences.en: Oh, that's really clear.
sentences.zh: 哦，这真的很清楚。

sentences.en: It's really sharp.
sentences.zh: 真的很敏锐。

sentences.en: The oh crap moment is November 1923.
sentences.zh: 那个“糟糕了”的时刻是1923年11月。

sentences.en: Love that.
sentences.zh: 喜欢这个说法。

sentences.en: So what happened then?
sentences.zh: 那么当时发生了什么？

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So Cincinnati residents got a referendum on the ballot to be voted on in November for a speed governor.
sentences.zh: 辛辛那提的居民在11月的选票上获得了一项关于限速器的公投。

sentences.en: A device built into the engine.
sentences.zh: 一种内置在发动机里的装置。

sentences.en: That would require cars to be equipped with one that would limit them to 25 miles an hour.
sentences.zh: 要求汽车必须配备这种装置，将其速度限制在每小时25英里。

sentences.en: And once the speed governor was there, it had a police seal on it.
sentences.zh: 一旦安装了限速器，上面会有警察的封条。

sentences.en: If you tampered with it, you were in violation of the law.
sentences.zh: 如果你篡改它，你就违反了法律。

sentences.en: This had lots of popular support.
sentences.zh: 这得到了广泛的民众支持。

sentences.en: We know 40,000 signatures on petitions.
sentences.zh: 我们知道请愿书上有40,000个签名。

sentences.en: You know, can't swear that they were all real people or so on, but there were 40,000 signatures on the petitions.
sentences.zh: 你知道，不能保证它们都是真实的人等等，但请愿书上确实有40,000个签名。

sentences.en: They had newspaper advertisements saying vote yes on this.
sentences.zh: 他们有报纸广告呼吁投赞成票。

sentences.en: This really woke up people who wanted a future for cars in cities.
sentences.zh: 这确实唤醒了那些希望汽车在城市中有未来的人。

sentences.en: They were worried that if cities had laws that restricted the use of cars, that people would stop buying them and opt for public transportation instead.
sentences.zh: 他们担心如果城市有限制汽车使用的法律，人们会停止购买汽车，转而选择公共交通。

sentences.en: Cars would be relegated to the countryside where fewer and fewer people lived every year.
sentences.zh: 汽车将被放逐到乡村，而那里居住的人口每年都在减少。

sentences.en: And this group of interests got organized and even gave themselves a name.
sentences.zh: 这群利益相关者组织起来，甚至给自己起了一个名字。

sentences.en: They call themselves Motordom.
sentences.zh: 他们称自己为“汽车王国”。

sentences.en: Motordom.
sentences.zh: 汽车王国。

sentences.en: Actually, that sounds pretty benign to my ears.
sentences.zh: 其实，在我听来这听起来相当温和。

sentences.en: Anyway.
sentences.zh: 不管怎样。

sentences.en: And they start to make distinctions between what they want and what the other safety advocates wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们开始区分他们想要的和那些安全倡导者想要的。

sentences.en: So you start to see, like in the Cincinnati Inquirer, which was sort of a mouthpiece for the auto industry in Cincinnati,
sentences.zh: 所以你开始看到，比如在《辛辛那提问询报》上，它算是辛辛那提汽车行业的喉舌，

sentences.en: they ran a huge amount of their advertising was from auto dealers.
sentences.zh: 他们刊登了大量来自汽车经销商的广告。

sentences.en: The Cincinnati Inquirer at one point says, the cause of accidents is men, not machines.
sentences.zh: 《辛辛那提问询报》有一次说，事故的原因是人，而不是机器。

sentences.en: In other words, cars don't kill people.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，汽车不会杀人。

sentences.en: People kill people.
sentences.zh: 是人杀人。

sentences.en: Which is reminiscent of an NRA motto that's been around for quite some time.
sentences.zh: 这让人想起了一个存在已久的美国全国步枪协会（NRA）的座右铭。

sentences.en: You know, guns don't kill people, people kill people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，枪不会杀人，人杀人。

sentences.en: It's the same basic idea.
sentences.zh: 这是同样的基本逻辑。

sentences.en: You can exonerate the machine if you blame the driver.
sentences.zh: 如果你责怪司机，你就可以为机器开脱。

sentences.en: And it wasn't so much about blaming the driver.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是关于责怪司机。

sentences.en: It was about promoting a subtle but super important distinction.
sentences.zh: 这是为了推广一个微妙但极其重要的区别。

sentences.en: The cause of accidents and deaths and children dying wasn't cars or speed.
sentences.zh: 事故、死亡和孩子丧生的原因不是汽车或速度。

sentences.en: It was recklessness.
sentences.zh: 那是一种鲁莽行为。

sentences.en: Cars could be perfectly safe in the streets.
sentences.zh: 街道本可以非常安全。

sentences.en: They belonged on the streets.
sentences.zh: 它们原本属于街道。

sentences.en: And the beauty of recklessness is that you could also be a reckless pedestrian.
sentences.zh: 而鲁莽的美妙之处在于，你也可以成为一名鲁莽的行人。

sentences.en: This is really important.
sentences.zh: 这一点非常重要。

sentences.en: What motoredom did by suggesting that pedestrians could be reckless could be the cause of accidents was start a turf war.
sentences.zh: “汽车王国”通过暗示行人鲁莽可能是事故起因，从而引发了一场领地之争。

sentences.en: A street fight.
sentences.zh: 一场街头斗争。

sentences.en: The oh crap moment in 1923 creates a clear sense in motoredom that they have to change the problem from how do we control cars and drivers into how do we make streets places where cars belong and where pedestrians don't belong.
sentences.zh: 1923 年的“糟糕时刻”让汽车王国明确意识到，他们必须将问题从“如何控制汽车和司机”转变为“如何让街道成为汽车的领地，而非行人的领地”。

sentences.en: Motoredom needed to market the idea that accidents could be the result of reckless pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 汽车王国需要推销一种观念，即事故可能是由鲁莽的行人造成的。

sentences.en: And even that there was such a thing as reckless pedestrians, which people weren't ready to accept yet.
sentences.zh: 甚至要推销“鲁莽行人”这一概念，而当时人们还没准备好接受这一点。

sentences.en: One judge in particular angrily denounced the idea that you could ever have such a thing as a reckless pedestrian.
sentences.zh: 一位法官曾愤怒地谴责这种说法，认为根本不存在所谓的“鲁莽行人”。

sentences.en: So to sell the idea of reckless pedestrians, motoredom invented a new word.
sentences.zh: 因此，为了推销“鲁莽行人”的概念，汽车王国发明了一个新词。

sentences.en: Jaywalking.
sentences.zh: “乱穿马路者”（Jaywalking）。

sentences.en: Well, actually, they didn't invent it.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实他们并没有发明这个词。

sentences.en: Motoredom repurposed a word that had been kicking around for a couple of decades.
sentences.zh: 汽车王国重新利用了一个已经流传了几十年的词。

sentences.en: They transformed it from a slang insult to a legal term.
sentences.zh: 他们将其从一种俚语侮辱变成了法律术语。

sentences.en: In the 19-teens, Jay, J-A-Y, was a word for country bumpkin.
sentences.zh: 在 1910 年代，“Jay”这个词指的是乡巴佬。

sentences.en: Therefore, a Jaywalker is somebody who walks around the city like a Jay from the sticks.
sentences.zh: 因此，“Jaywalker”就是指那些像乡下人一样在城市里乱走的人。

sentences.en: Well, the first actually clear illustration of what the word means that I found is from Kansas City, 1911.
sentences.zh: 我找到的关于这个词含义的最清晰的解释，来自 1911 年的堪萨斯城。

sentences.en: And there it's describing, and they actually have a cartoon that shows a Jaywalker.
sentences.zh: 那里有一幅漫画，展示了一个“Jaywalker”。

sentences.en: They're describing the Jaywalker there as exactly that.
sentences.zh: 他们对“Jaywalker”的描述正是如此。

sentences.en: The person from the countryside who's in the big city and is so dazzled by the show windows, the lights, the tall buildings, the salesmen, and so on,
sentences.zh: 指那些从乡下来到大城市的人，被橱窗、灯光、高楼、推销员等等迷得眼花缭乱，

sentences.en: that as they're walking on the sidewalk, they're constantly stopping to look and thereby obstructing other pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 以至于在人行道上走的时候，他们不断停下来观看，从而阻碍了其他行人。

sentences.en: So there, a Jaywalker is really a nuisance to other pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 所以，那时的“Jaywalker”实际上是对其他行人的干扰。

sentences.en: So Motoredom took this word that had meant a kind of annoying pedestrian and gave it a new meaning,
sentences.zh: 于是，汽车王国拿走了这个原本指代“烦人行人”的词，并赋予了它新的含义，

sentences.en: a pedestrian who breaks the traffic rules, who enters the streets in the wrong place or at the wrong time.
sentences.zh: 即指那些违反交通规则，在错误的时间或地点进入街道的行人。

sentences.en: They did this by publishing editorials about Jaywalking.
sentences.zh: 他们通过发表关于“乱穿马路”的社论来做到这一点。

sentences.en: Auto clubs and auto dealers got Boy Scouts in a number of cities to hand out little cards that would say something like,
sentences.zh: 汽车俱乐部和汽车经销商让许多城市的童子军分发小卡片，上面写着类似的话：

sentences.en: did you know you were Jaywalking?
sentences.zh: “你知道你在乱穿马路吗？”

sentences.en: And we know that people don't know what the word meant because it was carefully explained on the card with diagrams and information.
sentences.zh: 我们知道人们当时并不明白这个词的意思，因为卡片上用图表和信息进行了仔细解释。

sentences.en: And at first, the efforts to get people to stop doing something they had done for decades just didn't work.
sentences.zh: 起初，试图让人们停止他们几十年来一直习惯的行为的努力并没有奏效。

sentences.en: There was even an incident where, according to a newspaper, women struck police officers with their parasols for trying to control how they crossed the street.
sentences.zh: 甚至发生过这样的事：据报纸报道，有妇女因为警察试图管制她们过马路的方式，而用遮阳伞殴打警察。

sentences.en: The lesson for Motoredom was, you can't do this by law.
sentences.zh: 汽车王国得到的教训是：不能靠法律来强行推行。

sentences.en: But finally, Motoredom hit upon a winning strategy, devised by E.B.
sentences.zh: 但最终，汽车王国想出了一种制胜策略，由 E.B. Lefferts 设计。

sentences.en: Lefferts.
sentences.zh: 莱弗茨。

sentences.en: E.B.
sentences.zh: E.B.

sentences.en: Lefferts, enemy of Jaywalkers everywhere.
sentences.zh: Lefferts，各地“乱穿马路者”的死敌。

sentences.en: He was the head of the Automobile Club of Southern California, and I think he was, ahead of his time, a real public relations genius,
sentences.zh: 他是南加州汽车俱乐部的负责人，我认为他是一位超越时代的公关天才，

sentences.en: a guy who realized before most others did that you can't just change behavior by punishing people and putting laws up.
sentences.zh: 他比大多数人更早意识到，你不能仅仅通过惩罚人们和制定法律来改变行为。

sentences.en: You have to reach them through psychology.
sentences.zh: 你必须通过心理学来影响他们。

sentences.en: Lefferts created a PR campaign in Los Angeles explaining what jaywalking was,
sentences.zh: Lefferts 在洛杉矶发起了一场公关运动，解释什么是乱穿马路，

sentences.en: and he helped get an anti-jaywalking ordinance passed in 1924.
sentences.zh: 并推动在 1924 年通过了一项禁止乱穿马路的法令。

sentences.en: But here's the really clever part.
sentences.zh: 但最聪明的地方在于：

sentences.en: He told the police not to arrest jaywalkers.
sentences.zh: 他告诉警察不要逮捕乱穿马路的人。

sentences.en: Lefferts wanted the police officer not to arrest the jaywalker, which would only make the jaywalker indignant,
sentences.zh: Lefferts 希望警察不要逮捕乱穿马路者，因为那只会让对方感到愤慨，

sentences.en: but to attract ridicule.
sentences.zh: 而是要引发嘲笑。

sentences.en: And he uses the word ridicule.
sentences.zh: 他确实用了“嘲笑”这个词。

sentences.en: Oh, there's a gap in the traffic.
sentences.zh: 哦，车流中有个空档。

sentences.en: I'd just pop over to the druggist for some cannabis.
sentences.zh: 我正好去药店买点大麻。

sentences.en: Here we are.
sentences.zh: 到了。

sentences.en: Hey, you, out of the street.
sentences.zh: 嘿，你，离开马路。

sentences.en: Don't you realize you're jaywalking?
sentences.zh: 你不知道你在乱穿马路吗？

sentences.en: What, me?
sentences.zh: 什么，我？

sentences.en: A jaywalker?
sentences.zh: 乱穿马路者？

sentences.en: What would my mother think?
sentences.zh: 我妈会怎么想？

sentences.en: Lefferts wanted the pedestrian ridiculed as a form of psychological control.
sentences.zh: Lefferts 希望通过嘲笑行人来作为一种心理控制手段。

sentences.en: And to Lefferts, it was more important that the onlookers see this person being ridiculed
sentences.zh: 对 Lefferts 来说，让旁观者看到这个人被嘲笑，

sentences.en: than that you actually sort of convert this individual to correct crossing behavior.
sentences.zh: 比真正让这个人改掉过马路的习惯更重要。

sentences.en: The onlookers are going to witness this ridicule and think, I don't want to get that kind of
sentences.zh: 旁观者会目睹这种嘲笑，心想：我可不想受到那种嘲笑，

sentences.en: ridicule, so I'm going to cross carefully.
sentences.zh: 所以我还是小心过马路吧。

sentences.en: That's fiendishly clever.
sentences.zh: 这真是极其阴险的聪明。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's a little hard to relate to now because jaywalker is sort of a benign word, like loitering.
sentences.zh: 现在很难产生共鸣，因为“乱穿马路”现在听起来像“游荡”一样是个中性词。

sentences.en: But in 1920s America, it was a real term of abuse.
sentences.zh: 但在 20 世纪 20 年代的美国，这确实是一个侮辱性词汇。

sentences.en: And actually, several judges and newspaper editors objected to the use of such an insulting
sentences.zh: 事实上，几位法官和报纸编辑都反对对行人使用这种侮辱性词汇。

sentences.en: term for pedestrians.
sentences.zh: 它带有“白痴”的含义。

sentences.en: It carried the connotation of idiot.
sentences.zh: 我想如果你今天发起一场公共安全运动，内容是称呼人们为白痴，

sentences.en: I think if you were trying to sort of have a public safety campaign that involved calling
sentences.zh: 你也会遇到类似的反应。

sentences.en: people idiots, you would find a similar kind of reaction today.
sentences.zh: 你知道，人们真的会反对那样做。

sentences.en: You know, people would really object to that.
sentences.zh: 或者想象一些更现代的情况。

sentences.en: Or imagine something even more contemporary.
sentences.zh: 哦，车流中有个空档。

sentences.en: Oh, there's a gap in the traffic.
sentences.zh: 我正好去药店买点大麻。

sentences.en: I'd just pop over to the druggist for some cannabis.
sentences.zh: 到了。

sentences.en: Here we are.
sentences.zh: 哈？

sentences.en: Huh?
sentences.zh: 嘿，你，离开马路。

sentences.en: Hey you, out of the street.
sentences.zh: 你不知道你在做“混蛋行为”吗？

sentences.en: Don't you realize you're douchebagging?
sentences.zh: 嘿，看那个混蛋。

sentences.en: Hey, look at that douchebag.
sentences.zh: 跳得真高。

sentences.en: What a jump.
sentences.zh: 什么，我？

sentences.en: What, me?
sentences.zh: 混蛋？

sentences.en: A douchebag?
sentences.zh: 我妈会怎么想？

sentences.en: What would my mother think?
sentences.zh: 关键是，嘲笑奏效了。

sentences.en: The thing is, the ridicule worked.
sentences.zh: 报纸报道显示，仅仅几周后，洛杉矶的行人就明白了其中的含义。

sentences.en: Newspaper reports show that just after a few weeks, pedestrians in L.A.
sentences.zh: 街道被清理出来留给了汽车。

sentences.en: got the message.
sentences.zh: Peter Norton 说，到 1929 年，汽车王国可以宣布胜利了。

sentences.en: And the streets were cleared for cars.
sentences.zh: 巧合的是，或者也许并非巧合，那一年美国建成了第一个苜蓿叶形立交桥，

sentences.en: Peter Norton says motordom could declare victory by 1929.
sentences.zh: 巩固了美国与汽车的未来。

sentences.en: Coincidentally, or maybe not so coincidentally, this was the year the first Cloverleaf interchange
sentences.zh: 顺便提一下，大约在那个时候，人们不再反对“乱穿马路者”这个词，

sentences.en: was built in the United States, cementing the country's future with automobiles.
sentences.zh: 包括乱穿马路者自己，法官们也不再抵制这个词了。

sentences.en: Incidentally, that's around the time that you find that people stop objecting to the term
sentences.zh: 新的城市街道在建设时也考虑到了汽车。

sentences.en: jaywalker, including jaywalkers themselves, and, you know, judges are no longer resisting that.
sentences.zh: 街道变得更宽以容纳更多汽车。

sentences.en: And new city streets are built with cars in mind.
sentences.zh: 新企业被要求提供停车场。

sentences.en: The streets get wider to accommodate more cars.
sentences.zh: 人行横道成为强制性设施。

sentences.en: New businesses are required to provide parking lots.
sentences.zh: 城市开始修建高速公路，以便汽车进出城市更加方便。

sentences.en: Crosswalks become compulsory.
sentences.zh: 值得花点时间反思一下这个故事是如何被讲述的。

sentences.en: And cities start building expressways to make it easier to get cars in and out of cities.
sentences.zh: George Orwell 曾解释说，历史是由胜利者书写的。

sentences.en: And it's worth taking a moment to reflect on how this story has been told.
sentences.zh: 因为在书写历史的过程中，你是在为自己辩护。

sentences.en: George Orwell explained that history is written by the winners.
sentences.zh: 因此，汽车的历史并非由某个人，而是随着时间推移被集体书写出来的，

sentences.en: Because in writing the history, you justify yourself.
sentences.zh: 这在很大程度上是一部胜利者的汽车史。

sentences.en: So, a history of the automobile has been written, not by any single individual, but collectively
sentences.zh: 这就是那种认为一切都是“不可避免”的历史。

sentences.en: over time, that predominantly is a winner's history of the automobile.
sentences.zh: 这与美国对汽车的“热爱”有关。

sentences.en: And that's the history that says this was inevitable.
sentences.zh: 在早些年，美国似乎并没有对汽车表现出那种狂热的激情。

sentences.en: And it has to do with America's love affair with the automobile.
sentences.zh: 那绝对不是一见钟情。

sentences.en: In those early years, it hardly seemed that America had a consuming passion for the automobile.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你知道是什么让汽车开始流行起来的吗？

sentences.en: It certainly wasn't love at first sight.
sentences.zh: 和让某些女孩受欢迎的原因一样。

sentences.en: In fact, do you know what first began to make the car popular?
sentences.zh: 她们因为“快”而闻名。

sentences.en: The same thing that made some girls popular.
sentences.zh: 1961 年，有一个电视节目叫《杜邦周刊》，它自称是一部纪录片电视节目。

sentences.en: They got a reputation for being faSt.
sentences.zh: 当时杜邦公司拥有通用汽车三分之一的股份。

sentences.en: In 1961, there was a TV program called the DuPont Show of the Week, which represented itself as a documentary TV show.
sentences.zh: 所以，这两家公司有很多共同点。

sentences.en: And DuPont at that time had a one-third interest in General Motors.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们写了一集名为《我们快乐地前行》的节目，讲述了美国的汽车史。

sentences.en: So, the two companies had a lot in common.
sentences.zh: 他们请了 Groucho Marx 来主持。

sentences.en: And so, they wrote an episode called Merrily We Roll Along, which was a history of the automobile in the United States.
sentences.zh: 在这个节目中，Groucho Marx 向美国人介绍了我们都听过的那个论点，

sentences.en: They got Groucho Marx to host it.
sentences.zh: 即美国人与汽车之间存在着一场“爱情故事”。

sentences.en: And in this show, Groucho Marx introduced Americans to the thesis we've all heard,
sentences.zh: 我们愉快地唱着关于汽车的歌，一起在生活中穿梭，

sentences.en: which is that there is an American love affair with the automobile.
sentences.zh: 开始了与我们新爱人的漫长蜜月。

sentences.en: We sang blithely about automobile bubbling through life together
sentences.zh: 如果她有什么缺点，那就是稍微有点脾气。

sentences.en: and started out on the long honeymoon with our new sweetheart.
sentences.zh: 这就是“爱情故事”论点。

sentences.en: If she had any fault, it was a slight crankiness.
sentences.zh: 它的天才之处在于，通过说我们与汽车有“爱情故事”，

sentences.en: So, that's the love affair thesis.
sentences.zh: 我们是在说我们的关系是不理性的，不受逻辑判断的约束。

sentences.en: And the genius of it is that by saying we have a love affair with the car,
sentences.zh: 如果那不是婚姻，我不知道什么才是。

sentences.en: we are saying that our relationship is irrational and not subject to logical judgment.
sentences.zh: 我们一起经历了两次战争和一次大萧条。

sentences.en: And if that isn't marriage, I don't know what is.
sentences.zh: 她载着我们飞越了航空时代，进入了原子时代。

sentences.en: We've been through two wars together and a depression.
sentences.zh: 无论我们现在要去哪里，都会乘坐像这样的交通工具。

sentences.en: She's carried us through the air age and into the atomic age.
sentences.zh: 它可能是核动力的、雷达控制的、陀螺稳定的，还富含维生素。

sentences.en: Wherever we're headed now, it'll be in something like this.
sentences.zh: 但它会有前后车牌、前灯和喇叭。

sentences.en: It may be nuclear-powered, radar-controlled, gyro-stead, and vitamin-enriched.
sentences.zh: 偶尔，我们还是得下车推它一把。

sentences.en: But, it'll have license plates front or back, headlights and a horn.
sentences.zh: 所以，我们快乐地前行。

sentences.en: And once in a while, we'll still have to get out and give it a shove.
sentences.zh: 甚至连汽车的批评者，包括我在内，

sentences.en: So, merrily we roll along.
sentences.zh: 都接受了这种美国人与汽车有“爱情故事”的观点。

sentences.en: And even critics of cars, including me,
sentences.zh: 因为汽车的批评者会说，

sentences.en: we've bought into this idea of an American love affair with the automobile.
sentences.zh: 你看，这种爱情故事，

sentences.en: Because the critics of the automobile could say,
sentences.zh: 这种我们对汽车的文化依恋才是问题所在。

sentences.en: you know, look, this love affair,
sentences.zh: 这完全分散了他们的注意力，使他们忽略了一个事实：

sentences.en: this cultural attachment we have to the automobile is the problem.
sentences.zh: 20 世纪 20 年代变革的真实故事要复杂得多，

sentences.en: Which completely distracted them from the fact
sentences.zh: 事实上，其中包含了对汽车的很多仇恨。

sentences.en: that the actual story of the transformation of the 1920s
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你在 20 年代看到了对汽车真正的妖魔化，

sentences.en: was a lot more complicated
sentences.zh: 而这些已经被完全遗忘了。

sentences.en: and, in fact, involved a lot of hate of the car.
sentences.zh: 没人记得那些纪念汽车受害者的活动。

sentences.en: I mean, you see real demonization of the car in the 20s
sentences.zh: 没人记得那些纪念碑。

sentences.en: that's been totally forgotten.
sentences.zh: 没人记得那些由撒旦驾驶 T 型车的游行。

sentences.en: Nobody remembers the memorials to the car.
sentences.zh: 没人记得那些漫画，那些社论漫画，

sentences.en: Nobody remembers the monuments.
sentences.zh: 经常把汽车比作死神、摩洛神和主宰者等等。

sentences.en: Nobody remembers the parades with Satan driving a Model T.
sentences.zh: 美国人确实爱汽车，这是真的。

sentences.en: Nobody remembers the cartoons, the editorial cartoons
sentences.zh: 但我们如此热爱汽车的部分原因，

sentences.en: that routinely compared cars to the Grim Reaper
sentences.zh: 是因为我们的城市是按照汽车的需求重建的。

sentences.en: and Moloch and Juggernaut and all that.
sentences.zh: 我们有停车场。

sentences.en: And it's true that Americans love cars.
sentences.zh: 我们有停车场。

sentences.en: But part of the reason we love cars so much
sentences.zh: 我们有停车场。

sentences.en: is our cities have been rebuilt with cars in mind.
sentences.zh: 我们有停车场。

sentences.en: We have parking.
sentences.zh: 我们有停车场。

sentences.en: We have expressways.
sentences.zh: 我们有高速公路。

sentences.en: We don't have a lot of pedestrians getting in our way
sentences.zh: 我们没有那么多行人挡道，

sentences.en: and slowing us down.
sentences.zh: 也不会因此放慢速度。

sentences.en: And it may be changing.
sentences.zh: 这种情况或许正在改变。

sentences.en: But for the moment,
sentences.zh: 但就目前而言，

sentences.en: we still seem to like it that way.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎还是喜欢这样。

sentences.en: Sam Greenspan, and me, Roman Mars.
sentences.zh: Sam Greenspan 和我 Roman Mars 制作。

sentences.zh: Stephanie Fu、Julia DeWitt 和 Will Urbina。

sentences.en: You guys listening to this all listen to Snap Judgment, right?

sentences.zh: 当然听。

sentences.en: We are a project of 91.7 local public radio KALW in San Francisco

sentences.zh: 也是旧金山美国建筑师协会的项目。
